q: An electron starts from rest and travels through a potential difference of $500\,\text{V}$. How large is its kinetic energy in electronvolts and in joules?
a: The field does the work $eU$, so $E_\text{k} = 500\,\text{eV} = 500 \cdot 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J} \approx 8.0 \cdot 10^{-17}\,\text{J}$. The electron moves towards the higher potential, and its potential energy decreases by the same amount.

q: The voltage of a capacitor connected to a source is doubled. By what factor do its charge and energy change?
a: The capacitance does not change, so $Q = CU$ doubles and $W = \tfrac12 CU^2$ becomes four times as large, because the energy is proportional to the square of the voltage.
